questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair of cropping season and related crop from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabi - Paddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Paddy (rice)** is predominantly a **Kharif crop**, grown during the monsoon season due to its high water requirement.
 
• Kharif crops are typically sown at the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in the autumn (September-October).
 
• Rabi crops, such as wheat and mustard, are grown in the winter season and harvested in the spring (March-April).
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include paddy, maize, soyabean, and cotton, whereas Rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, and gram.
 
• The pairing of "Rabi - Paddy" is incorrect as paddy is not suited for the low rainfall and cooler conditions of the Rabi season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Crops:**

 
 
• These crops are sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in spring (March-April).
 
• They require cool weather for growth and less water compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Examples: Wheat, barley, mustard, peas, and gram.
 
 
 
• **Kharif Crops:**
 
 
• Sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October).
 
• They require hot and humid weather with substantial rainfall.
 
• Examples: Paddy, maize, soyabean, cotton, and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Crops:**
 
 
• Crops in India are broadly classified into three types based on the season: Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid.
 
• Zaid crops are grown between Rabi and Kharif seasons (March to June), e.g., watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops.
 
 
 
• **Water Requirements for Paddy:**
 
 
• Paddy is a water-intensive crop that requires standing water for growth.
 
• It thrives in areas with heavy rainfall or where irrigation facilities are available.

questions.question: R Muthukannammal, who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022, is a ____________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sadir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **R Muthukannammal** is a renowned practitioner of Sadir, an ancient classical dance form from Tamil Nadu.
 
• Sadir was traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotion to deities and is closely linked with the temple culture of South India.
 
• Muthukannammal belongs to the **Devadasi tradition**, which upheld this dance form for centuries.
 
• She has been instrumental in preserving and promoting the heritage of Sadir despite the decline of the Devadasi system.
 
• For her exceptional contributions to Indian classical dance, she was awarded the **Padma Shri in 2022**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sadir:**

 
 
• Sadir is also referred to as the predecessor to Bharatanatyam, which evolved later as a more codified form of the dance.
 
• It involves intricate footwork, graceful movements, and facial expressions to narrate stories, usually from Hindu mythology.
 
• The dance form was primarily performed by Devadasis, women dedicated to temple service, as an offering to the divine.
 
 
 
• **Devadasi Tradition:**
 
 
• The Devadasi system was a historical practice in which women were dedicated to temples and played a significant role in the preservation of art forms like Sadir.
 
• With societal changes and legal reforms in the 20th century, the system declined, leading to a reduced practice of Sadir.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri:**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contributions across various fields.
 
• Muthukannammal received the Padma Shri in 2022 for her lifelong dedication to the art of Sadir.
 
 
 
• **Revival Efforts:**
 
 
• Efforts are ongoing to revive Sadir and bring it to mainstream recognition as a classical dance form.
 
• Artists like Muthukannammal are central to these revival movements, ensuring the continuity of cultural heritage.

questions.question: The word 'Megalith' comes from two _____ words; 'megas' means great and 'lithas' means stone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The word 'Megalith' is derived from the **Greek language**, combining "megas" (meaning great) and "lithos" (meaning stone).
 
• Megaliths are large stone structures or monuments created by ancient civilizations for various purposes, such as burials or rituals.
 
• The term is widely used in archaeology to describe prehistoric monuments like dolmens, menhirs, and stone circles.
 
• Examples of megalithic structures include Stonehenge in England and Carnac stones in France.
 
• The study of megaliths provides valuable insights into the engineering, culture, and beliefs of early human societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dolmen:** A type of megalithic tomb usually consisting of a large flat stone supported by upright stones. Also called portal tombs.
 
• **Menhir:** A single upright stone, often of great size, erected in prehistoric times, commonly found in Europe.
 
• **Stone Circles:** Circular arrangements of megaliths, such as Stonehenge, often associated with astronomical or ceremonial purposes.
 
• **Megalithic Culture:** Refers to the period in prehistory when large stone monuments were constructed, usually during the Neolithic or Bronze Age.
 
• **Archaeological Significance:** Megalithic structures often serve as evidence of early human ingenuity, social organization, and spiritual practices.

questions.question: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person whose weight is 50 kg and height is 1.5 m.
questions.solution:

• **Definition of BMI:** BMI stands for Body Mass Index, a measure that uses height and weight to estimate body fat.
 
• **Purpose of BMI:** It is used to classify individuals into categories such as underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obese.
 
• **Limitations of BMI:** BMI does not differentiate between muscle and fat mass and may not accurately reflect health status for highly muscular individuals or the elderly.

questions.question: Which of the following is an Indian folk dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is a traditional folk dance of Assam, performed during the Assamese New Year celebrations, known as **Bihu festivals** (Rongali Bihu).
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women, showcasing vibrant movements, synchronized steps, and rhythmic clapping, accompanied by traditional instruments like the **dhol** (drum) and **pepa** (bamboo flute).
 
• Bihu dance is an integral part of Assamese culture and heritage, symbolizing joy, unity, and the arrival of the harvest season.
 
• It is a non-religious, community-oriented performance and is recognized as a celebration of life and nature.
 
• Unlike classical dances, Bihu is characterized by its free-spirited and energetic movements, reflecting the exuberance of Assamese rural life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and hand gestures (mudras).
 
• It is one of the oldest Indian classical dance forms and was traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**
 
 
• A classical dance form from Kerala, Mohiniyattam is characterized by graceful, swaying movements and a focus on feminine themes.
 
• The name "Mohiniyattam" refers to the dance of the enchantress, derived from the word "Mohini," a mythical female avatar of Lord Vishnu.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• A classical dance form from Assam, Sattriya was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century as a part of religious rituals.
 
• It is performed as an offering to Lord Krishna in the Sattras (Vaishnavite monasteries).
 
 
 
• **Difference between Folk and Classical Dance**
 
 
• **Folk dances** are community-based, informal, and reflect the traditions and lifestyle of a specific region (e.g., Bihu, Garba).
 
• **Classical dances** have a codified structure, are deeply rooted in religious and spiritual themes, and follow strict rules (e.g., Bharatanatyam, Kathak).

questions.question: Which country won the 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023 event in the Men's category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won the **4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023** in the Men's category, held in **Tamulpur, Assam**.
 
• The Indian men's team defeated **Nepal** in the finals to secure the championship title.
 
• The event featured **participation from 12 countries**, showcasing competitive matches throughout the tournament.
 
• India displayed exceptional skill and teamwork, reinforcing its dominance in the sport of Kho-Kho.
 
• This victory further strengthens India's position as a leading nation in traditional sports such as Kho-Kho.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kho-Kho** is a traditional Indian sport known for its fast-paced nature and emphasis on agility, teamwork, and strategy.
 
• The sport is played between two teams, with players alternating between chasing (defenders) and running (attackers).
 
• The **Asian Kho-Kho Federation** governs the sport at the continental level and organizes championships like the Asian Kho-Kho Championship.
 
• Kho-Kho is gaining international recognition and is being promoted as part of India's efforts to popularize indigenous sports globally.
 
• The 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023 was hosted in **India** to further boost the visibility and development of the sport.

questions.question: Where was Global Technology Summit 2022 held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Global Technology Summit 2022 was held in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• It was co-hosted by the **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)**, Government of India, and Carnegie India.
 
• The event is an annual flagship initiative that focuses on examining the intersection of **technology, economics, and foreign policy**.
 
• The 2022 theme was **"Geopolitics of Technology"**, addressing critical global challenges and opportunities in the tech landscape.
 
• It brought together global policymakers, industry leaders, academia, and researchers to discuss the future of technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Technology Summit**

 
 
• The summit is one of the most prominent forums in India for discussing the role of technology in shaping global policies.
 
• It provides a platform for fostering collaboration between governments and the private sector to address shared challenges.
 
• The event is known for its focus on emerging technologies such as AI, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and space technologies.
 
• Previous editions have emphasized India's growing role in the global technological ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Carnegie India**
 
 
• It is a premier think tank based in New Delhi, part of the global Carnegie Endowment for International Peace network.
 
• Carnegie India works on issues related to technology policy, security studies, and political economy.
 
• The organization is known for its deep engagement with policymakers and thought leaders globally.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitics of Technology**
 
 
• This concept explores how technology shapes and is shaped by global political and economic power dynamics.
 
• Key areas include competition in AI, semiconductor supply chains, digital trade policies, and the regulation of big tech companies.
 
• The summit highlights how nations can leverage technology to achieve strategic and economic objectives.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in Technology Diplomacy**
 
 
• India is increasingly positioning itself as a global leader in technology and innovation.
 
• Initiatives such as the Digital India campaign and Aadhaar have showcased India's ability to implement large-scale tech solutions.
 
• India's participation in global tech forums underscores its commitment to shaping the future of technology governance.

questions.question: The Ganesh-rath is one of the finest monolithic temples at __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabalipuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ganesh-rath is a monolithic rock-cut temple located in **Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu**, India, also known as Mamallapuram.
 
• It is part of the **Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.
 
• The temple is carved out of a single granite rock and is dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, although it later came to be associated with Lord Ganesha.
 
• Constructed during the **Pallava dynasty** in the 7th century under King Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), it reflects the Dravidian architectural style.
 
• The Ganesh-rath is one of the **five rathas (chariots)** that exhibit the evolution of South Indian temple architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram:**

 
 
• Mahabalipuram hosts several monuments including rock-cut temples, cave sanctuaries, and giant open-air relief sculptures.
 
• These monuments were built during the **Pallava dynasty**, primarily in the 7th and 8th centuries.
 
• Other notable structures include the Shore Temple, Arjuna’s Penance, and the Five Rathas.
 
• They showcase a blend of **artistic innovation and architectural excellence**.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture:**
 
 
• A distinct style of temple architecture originating in Southern India during ancient times.
 
• Characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (vimanas), intricate carvings, and monolithic structures.
 
• The Pallavas were among the first to pioneer this style, which was later refined by the Cholas, Pandyas, and Vijayanagara dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India from the 4th to 9th centuries CE.
 
• They are credited with pioneering rock-cut and structural temple architecture in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Notable kings include Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla).
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
 
• This recognition highlights its **historical significance and architectural brilliance**.

questions.question: Jyotiba Phule belonged from which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotiba Phule was born in **Maharashtra** on 11th April 1827 in Satara district.
 
• He was a prominent social reformer and thinker who worked towards the upliftment of the oppressed classes and women.
 
• Phule is widely recognized for his efforts in promoting education among marginalized sections of society, particularly through the establishment of the first girls' school in Pune, Maharashtra, in 1848.
 
• He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 in Maharashtra to fight caste discrimination and advocate social equality.
 
• Jyotiba Phule’s contributions to social reform earned him the title of **Mahatma**, meaning "great soul."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj**

 
 
• Founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873, the Satyashodhak Samaj aimed to create a society free from caste and gender discrimination.
 
• It advocated for rational thinking and the abolition of priestly dominance in religious practices.
 
• The organization encouraged self-respect and dignity among marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Educational Contributions**
 
 
• Jyotiba Phule and his wife, Savitribai Phule, were pioneers in women's education in India.
 
• They established the first girls' school in Pune in 1848, a revolutionary step during that era.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms**
 
 
• Phule worked tirelessly to eradicate caste-based discrimination and untouchability.
 
• He emphasized the importance of education as a tool for social reform and empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• Jyotiba Phule’s work laid the foundation for social movements advocating equality and justice in India.
 
• He is remembered as one of the most influential social reformers in Indian history.

questions.question: On 27th October 2019, Dushyant Chautala took an oath as Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dushyant Chautala** took the oath as Deputy Chief Minister of Haryana on **27th October 2019**.
 
• He is the leader of the **Jannayak Janta Party (JJP)**, a regional political party in Haryana.
 
• The oath ceremony was conducted following the formation of a coalition government between the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and JJP in Haryana after the 2019 assembly elections.
 
• Manohar Lal Khattar, from the BJP, was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Haryana for his second term on the same day.
 
• Dushyant Chautala is the grandson of former Haryana Chief Minister **Om Prakash Chautala** and represents the younger leadership in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haryana's Political Landscape**

 
 
• Haryana has a unicameral legislature with 90 members in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The state has been historically dominated by regional parties and leaders, especially the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) and its offshoot, JJP.
 
• The BJP emerged as a significant political force in Haryana in recent years, forming the government in 2014 and 2019.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Chief Minister Role**
 
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister assists the Chief Minister in governance and administration.
 
• In coalition governments, the Deputy Chief Minister often represents the interests of the coalition partner.
 
• The position is not mandatory, but it is created when deemed politically necessary.
 
 
 
• **2019 Haryana Assembly Elections**
 
 
• The elections were held on **21st October 2019**, and the results were declared on **24th October 2019**.
 
• No party secured an absolute majority; BJP won 40 seats, JJP won 10 seats, and the remaining seats were won by INC and independents.
 
• A coalition government was formed between BJP and JJP, with Dushyant Chautala becoming the Deputy CM.
 
 
 
• **Haryana State Overview**
 
 
• Haryana was carved out of Punjab on **1st November 1966**.
 
• It is known for its agricultural contributions, especially in wheat and rice production.
 
• Chandigarh serves as the shared capital of Haryana and Punjab.
 
• Haryana has a significant role in India's sports and defense sectors, producing many national-level athletes and soldiers.

questions.question: Where was the Hindu college established in the year 1791 to teach ancient Sanskrit texts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu College was established in **1791 in Banaras (modern-day Varanasi)** by the efforts of Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident of Banaras.
 
• The college aimed to **promote the study of ancient Sanskrit texts** and traditional Hindu learning.
 
• It was later renamed as the **Government Sanskrit College** and eventually became an important center of learning for classical Indian texts.
 
• The institution was primarily focused on teaching subjects like **philosophy, grammar, literature, and law** in Sanskrit.
 
• The Hindu College in Banaras is considered a forerunner to institutions like the **Benares Hindu University (BHU).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banaras (Varanasi)**

 
 
• Banaras, also known as Varanasi, is one of the **oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world**.
 
• It has been a major center for religion, culture, and education for centuries, particularly for Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Education in Ancient India**
 
 
• Sanskrit was the primary language of instruction in ancient Indian education systems.
 
• Subjects like philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, and medicine were taught using Sanskrit texts.
 
 
 
• **Jonathan Duncan**
 
 
• Jonathan Duncan was a British administrator who served as the Resident of Banaras from 1788 to 1795.
 
• He played a significant role in promoting Sanskrit education and setting up the Hindu College in Banaras.
 
 
 
• **Modern Education Evolution**
 
 
• The Hindu College of Banaras laid the foundation for modern educational institutions in India, such as the Benares Hindu University (BHU), established by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916.
 
• These institutions continue to contribute to the preservation and study of ancient Indian texts and traditions.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India marked the lowest in National Multi-dimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kerala recorded the **lowest multi-dimensional poverty index (MPI)** among all Indian states in the **National Multi-dimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023**.
 
• Only **0.7%** of Kerala's population was classified as multi-dimensionally poor, making it the best-performing state in this metric.
 
• The report, based on data from the **National Family Health Survey-5 (2019-2021)**, highlights Kerala's strong performance in health, education, and living standards.
 
• Kerala's achievements are attributed to its focus on **universal education, healthcare, and social welfare programs** over several decades.
 
• The state’s consistent investment in **human development** has enabled it to achieve low poverty levels compared to other states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• India's MPI is aligned with the global MPI developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions: **health, education, and living standards**, which are further divided into 12 indicators.
 
• Unlike income-based poverty measures, MPI captures the multiple deprivations that individuals face.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Human Development Model**
 
 
• Kerala is known for its **high literacy rate** (96.2% as per NFHS-5) and excellent public health indicators.
 
• The state has a strong network of public healthcare facilities and a focus on **primary education**.
 
• Social welfare programs, such as pensions for the elderly and marginalized groups, have significantly reduced poverty levels.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Performing States**
 
 
• States such as **Goa** and **Sikkim** also performed well, with relatively low levels of multi-dimensional poverty.
 
• These states have prioritized investments in education, healthcare, and infrastructure, contributing to better living standards.
 
 
 
• **Significance of MPI**
 
 
• The MPI provides a more comprehensive picture of poverty compared to traditional income-based measures.
 
• It helps policymakers identify areas that require targeted interventions for **poverty alleviation**.
 
• The data can also be used to track progress towards achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG-1 (No Poverty).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the capital receipts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax revenue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Capital receipts** are those receipts that lead to an increase in liabilities or decrease in assets of the government.
 
• Tax revenue, such as income tax, GST, and corporation tax, is categorized as **revenue receipts**, not capital receipts.
 
• Capital receipts include **borrowing, disinvestment, recovery of loans, and other non-tax revenue sources**.
 
• **Revenue receipts** consist of tax and non-tax revenues that do not create liabilities or decrease assets.
 
• Tax revenue is used to finance day-to-day expenditures and is not considered part of capital receipts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Receipts**

 
 
• Capital receipts represent funds raised by the government which create liabilities or reduce assets.
 
• Examples include loans raised from the public, foreign governments, or financial institutions, disinvestment proceeds, and recovery of loans.
 
• These are typically used for capital formation or repayment of liabilities.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts**
 
 
• Revenue receipts are income earned by the government without creating liabilities or reducing assets.
 
• They include tax revenues (e.g., income tax, GST) and non-tax revenues (e.g., fees, fines).
 
• These are used for day-to-day operational expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment**
 
 
• Disinvestment refers to the sale or liquidation of government assets, particularly public sector undertakings (PSUs).
 
• It is considered a capital receipt as it reduces government ownership and assets.
 
 
 
• **Borrowing**
 
 
• Borrowing includes loans raised by the government from domestic or international sources.
 
• It creates liabilities and is classified as a capital receipt.

questions.question: On boiling an egg, why does the outer part become opaque and white?

options.text: The heat causes a reaction of the egg with water and makes it opaque.
The heat causes a change in the crystal structure of egg yolk.
The heat causes a change in the structure of egg protein.
The heat causes denaturation, hardening the albumin and colouring it opaque white.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The heat causes denaturation, hardening the albumin and colouring it opaque white.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Egg whites contain proteins like ovalbumin, conalbumin, and ovotransferrin, which are normally folded in a specific structure.
 
• On heating, these proteins undergo a process called **denaturation**, where their natural structure unravels and they lose their solubility.
 
• The unfolded proteins then bond with each other, forming a solid network that traps water and turns the egg white opaque and white in color.
 
• Denaturation is a chemical reaction that alters the physical properties of proteins without breaking their primary structure.
 
• This process is irreversible and is responsible for the hardening and visual transformation of the egg white during boiling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein Denaturation:**

 
 
• Denaturation is the loss of the native structure of proteins due to external factors like heat, pH changes, or chemicals.
 
• It does not affect the primary sequence of amino acids but disrupts secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures.
 
• Common examples include cooking eggs, curdling milk, and the effects of alcohol on biological tissues.
 
 
 
• **Albumin:**
 
 
• Albumin is the main protein found in egg whites and plays a crucial role in the texture and appearance of cooked eggs.
 
• It is water-soluble and sensitive to temperature changes, making it ideal for cooking transformations.
 
 
 
• **Opaque Appearance:**
 
 
• The opaque white color of cooked egg whites is a result of light scattering caused by the dense protein network formed during denaturation.
 
• This network traps water molecules and alters the way light interacts with the surface.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Reaction:**
 
 
• The boiling process provides sufficient heat energy to break weak bonds in the protein molecules, triggering denaturation.
 
• The temperature required for denaturation of egg white proteins is approximately 60–70°C.

questions.question: Which of the following National Parks is located in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bandhavgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bandhavgarh National Park** is located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was declared a national park in **1968** and later became a Tiger Reserve under Project Tiger in **1993**.
 
• The park is renowned for its **high density of Bengal Tigers** and is one of the best places in India for tiger sightings.
 
• Bandhavgarh is also home to other fauna such as leopards, deer species, and over 250 species of birds.
 
• The park has historical significance due to the presence of the **ancient Bandhavgarh Fort**, believed to be over 2,000 years old.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Parks in Madhya Pradesh:**

 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is often called the **"Tiger State"** of India due to its significant tiger population.
 
• Other famous national parks in Madhya Pradesh include **Kanha National Park, Satpura National Park, and Pench National Park**.
 
• These parks are known for their rich biodiversity and serve as major tourist attractions for wildlife enthusiasts.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• A conservation initiative launched by the Government of India in **1973** to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
• Bandhavgarh is one of the reserves under this project aimed at increasing tiger populations in the country.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity of Bandhavgarh:**
 
 
• Bandhavgarh has a mix of deciduous forests, grasslands, and bamboo patches that support diverse flora and fauna.
 
• The park is home to species such as Sloth Bears, Indian Bison (Gaur), and several reptiles and amphibians.
 
 
 
• **Bandhavgarh Fort:**
 
 
• An ancient fort located within the park, believed to have been gifted by Lord Rama to his brother Lakshmana, as per Hindu mythology.
 
• The fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding forests and is of archaeological importance.

questions.question: Which of the following is the compound with the chemical formula H₂SO₄?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulfuric Acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sulfuric Acid (H₂SO₄)** is a highly corrosive strong acid widely used in industrial processes.
 
• It is commonly known as the "king of chemicals" due to its extensive applications in manufacturing and chemical synthesis.
 
• The chemical formula H₂SO₄ represents two hydrogen (H) atoms, one sulfur (S) atom, and four oxygen (O) atoms.
 
• Sulfuric acid is primarily used in the production of fertilizers, particularly phosphates and ammonium sulfate.
 
• It is also used in petroleum refining, chemical synthesis, wastewater processing, and as an electrolyte in lead-acid batteries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Properties of Sulfuric Acid:**

 
 
• It is a colorless to slightly yellow, odorless, and viscous liquid at room temperature.
 
• Highly soluble in water, but the dilution process is exothermic and must be done with caution.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• Highly corrosive to metals and tissues; direct contact can cause severe burns.
 
• Proper protective equipment, such as gloves and goggles, is essential when handling sulfuric acid.
 
 
 
• **Other Acids for Comparison:**
 
 
• **Nitric Acid (HNO₃):** Used in fertilizer production and explosives manufacturing.
 
• **Sulfurous Acid (H₂SO₃):** A weaker acid formed in aqueous sulfur dioxide.
 
• **Hydrogen Sulfide (H₂S):** A toxic gas, not an acid, with a characteristic rotten egg smell.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Industry:** Sulfuric acid is a key indicator of a nation's industrial strength due to its critical role in numerous sectors.

questions.question: According to Article 74(1), who is at the head of the Council of Ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the **Prime Minister** to aid and advise the President of India.
 
• The Prime Minister is the **chief executive authority** and plays a pivotal role in the functioning of the government.
 
• All major decisions of the government are taken by the Council of Ministers under the leadership of the Prime Minister.
 
• The President is constitutionally bound to act according to the advice provided by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (except in certain cases as per judicial interpretations).
 
• The Prime Minister is the leader of the ruling party or coalition in Parliament, thus providing a connection between the legislative and executive branches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President of India:**

 
 
• The President is the nominal executive and head of state as per the Constitution of India.
 
• He/she exercises powers based on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• In extraordinary circumstances, the President can use discretionary powers (e.g., appointment of the Prime Minister in case of a hung Parliament).
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and the leader of the Council of Ministers.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President and must command the confidence of the majority in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Prime Minister oversees the functioning of ministries and coordinates between different departments of the government.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers includes Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• They are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75 of the Constitution.
 
• The Council of Ministers works under the leadership of the Prime Minister to implement policies and administer governance.
 
 
 
• **Article 74:**
 
 
• Article 74 establishes the constitutional relationship between the President and the Council of Ministers.
 
• It ensures that the President exercises his/her functions based on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• This provision underscores the parliamentary system of governance in India.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Behdienkhlam Festival celebrated, in which the young men make a symbolic gesture of driving away of the evil spirit, plague and disease by beating the roof of every house with bamboo poles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Behdienkhlam Festival is celebrated in the state of **Meghalaya**, primarily by the Pnar tribal community of the Jaintia Hills region.
 
• The festival typically takes place in the month of **July**, marking the end of the sowing season and praying for a bountiful harvest.
 
• Young men perform symbolic rituals to drive away **evil spirits, plagues, and diseases** by beating the roofs of houses with bamboo poles.
 
• A key highlight of the festival is the traditional dance performed around a sacred pool, where logs called "Rots" are immersed as part of the ceremonies.
 
• The festival is deeply rooted in the cultural and religious beliefs of the Pnar people and showcases their reverence for nature and ancestral traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meaning of Behdienkhlam:** The name "Behdienkhlam" translates to "driving away the plague" in the Pnar language. It reflects the community's effort to ward off diseases and evil forces.
 
• **Ritual of Rots:** Wooden logs called "Rots" are decorated and carried through the village before being immersed in a sacred pool. This symbolizes unity and the collective effort to overcome challenges.
 
• **Ka Nohsni:** A special women-only dance called "Ka Nohsni" is performed during the festival, emphasizing the importance of women in Pnar society.
 
• **Religious Significance:** The festival is closely associated with the worship of the thunder god, known as "U Blei Shyllong," and other deities, seeking their blessings for prosperity and protection.
 
• **Tourism and Cultural Promotion:** The Behdienkhlam Festival has gained recognition as a major cultural event, attracting tourists and promoting Meghalaya's rich tribal heritage on a global stage.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities was the recipient of the Lata Mangeshkar Award for Music 2021, presented by the Madhya Pradesh government?

• The Madhya Pradesh government annually confers this award to individuals who have made significant contributions to Indian music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lata Mangeshkar Award**

questions.question: The first post-independence National Games were hosted by which of the following cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first post-independence National Games of India were held in **Lucknow**, the capital city of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This historic event took place in the year **1948**, marking the first National Games after India gained independence in 1947.
 
• The National Games were originally known as the **Indian Olympic Games**, which began in 1924, and were renamed post-independence.
 
• Lucknow was chosen as the host city due to its infrastructure and ability to organize large-scale events during that period.
 
• The National Games serve as a platform for athletes from across the country to showcase their talent and prepare for international sporting events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of the National Games of India**

 
 
• The National Games were initially modeled after the **Olympic Games** and were introduced to promote competitive sports in India.
 
• The first edition of the Indian Olympic Games was held in **Lahore in 1924**.
 
• Post-independence, the games were rebranded as the **National Games of India**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the National Games**
 
 
• They serve as a crucial selection ground for athletes aiming to represent India in international competitions, including the Olympics.
 
• The games are organized under the **aegis of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**.
 
 
 
• **Recent Editions of the National Games**
 
 
• The 36th National Games were held in **Gujarat** in 2022, showcasing over 6000 athletes across 36 sports disciplines.
 
• The games have seen significant improvements in infrastructure and athlete participation over the years.
 
 
 
• **Indian Olympic Movement**
 
 
• The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was established in **1927** to oversee the development of sports in India.
 
• The IOA is affiliated with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and plays a vital role in promoting sports and athletes in the country.

questions.question: The Hindu temples 'Hinglaj Mata' and 'Katasraj' are located in which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu temple **Hinglaj Mata** is located in the Hingol National Park in Balochistan, Pakistan, and is an important pilgrimage site for Hindus.
 
• The **Katasraj Temples**, also known as the Katas Raj Temples, are a complex of ancient Hindu temples located near Chakwal in Punjab, Pakistan.
 
• The Katasraj Temples are associated with Hindu mythology, believed to have been built around a sacred pond that was formed from the tears of Lord Shiva after the death of his wife, Sati.
 
• Hinglaj Mata is one of the **Shakti Peethas**, revered as holy sites where parts of Goddess Sati's body are believed to have fallen, as per Hindu mythology.
 
• Both Hinglaj Mata and Katasraj Temples are significant cultural and religious landmarks, attracting pilgrims from India and other countries despite political boundaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hinglaj Mata Shakti Peetha:**

 
 
• Hinglaj Mata is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where it is believed the head of Goddess Sati fell during Lord Shiva's Tandava.
 
• The site is located in a desert region and is visited by thousands of Hindu pilgrims annually, including during the Hinglaj Yatra.
 
• It is unique in that it is housed in a natural cave rather than a man-made structure.
 
 
 
• **Katasraj Temples:**
 
 
• The Katasraj complex includes several temples, some dating back to the Mahabharata era.
 
• The sacred pond, called **Katas**, is believed to have healing properties and is a major feature of the site.
 
• It is mentioned in Hindu texts like the Puranas and is also linked to the Pandavas' exile in Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance and Cultural Preservation in Pakistan:**
 
 
• Despite being a Muslim-majority country, Pakistan has preserved several Hindu and Sikh religious sites under its cultural heritage policies.
 
• Efforts are made to maintain these sites for religious pilgrims and as a part of the shared cultural history of the region.
 
 
 
• **Hindu Pilgrimage in Pakistan:**
 
 
• Hinglaj Mata and Katasraj Temples are among the key destinations for Hindu pilgrims traveling to Pakistan.
 
• Special arrangements are often made for pilgrims, including visas and security, under the bilateral agreements between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: The officer known as Diwan belonged to which of the following departments of the Mughal empire during Akbar's reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During Akbar's reign, the **Diwan** was the officer responsible for the **finance and revenue administration** of the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Diwan was tasked with the management of imperial finances, including the collection of taxes and disbursement of salaries to officials.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal**, one of Akbar's Navratnas, served as the Diwan and introduced the **revenue system known as "Zabt"** to streamline tax collection.
 
• The Diwan ensured proper record-keeping of income and expenditure through a system of ledgers and audits, maintaining fiscal discipline in the empire.
 
• Under Akbar’s administration, the finance department played a critical role in consolidating the empire’s economic foundation and ensuring efficient governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diwan's Role:**

 
 
• The term "Diwan" originates from Persian, meaning a register or office of accounts.
 
• The Diwan was considered the chief finance officer and reported directly to the emperor.
 
 
 
• **Zabt System:**
 
 
• The Zabt system assessed land revenue based on the average produce of land over a period of 10 years.
 
• This system was implemented in areas with a well-established agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Other Administrative Officers under Akbar:**
 
 
• **Mir Bakshi:** Responsible for military administration and payment of salaries to soldiers.
 
• **Sadr-us-Sudr:** Looked after religious endowments and judicial matters.
 
• **Qazi:** Acted as the chief judicial officer.
 
 
 
• **Akbar’s Administrative Reforms:**
 
 
• Akbar implemented a centralized administrative system, dividing the empire into provinces (Subahs).
 
• Each Subah was governed by a Subedar, with separate officials for revenue, military, and judicial functions.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles on Fundamental Duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51-A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51-A was added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• It introduced the concept of **Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens for the first time.
 
• There are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51-A, which outline the moral obligations of citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the **Soviet Constitution** and aim to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.
 
• This amendment was part of a series of changes during the Emergency period under the Indira Gandhi government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They were added to remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation and society.
 
• Examples include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it made to the Constitution.
 
• Introduced changes in the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and added Fundamental Duties.
 
• It strengthened the power of the central government and curtailed the authority of the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Inspiration from the Soviet Constitution**
 
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties in India was borrowed from the USSR (now Russia).
 
• The duties emphasize collective responsibility and the importance of national unity.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles vs Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Directive Principles guide the State in policy-making, while Fundamental Duties guide citizens in their conduct.
 
• Both aim to achieve a just and equitable society.

questions.question: The famous Hindi novel 'Maila Aanchal' is written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phanishwar Nath Renu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Maila Aanchal'** is a famous Hindi novel written by **Phanishwar Nath Renu**, a celebrated Indian writer.
 
• The novel was first published in **1954** and is considered a masterpiece of Hindi literature.
 
• **'Maila Aanchal'** is a regional novel that portrays the rural life, culture, and struggles of the people in a village in **north-eastern Bihar**.
 
• Phanishwar Nath Renu is known as the pioneer of the **'Aanchalik Upanyas' (Regional Novel)** tradition in Hindi literature.
 
• The novel is hailed for its authentic depiction of rural India and its use of local dialects, which add depth and realism to the narrative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phanishwar Nath Renu:**

 
 
• He was born on **4 March 1921** in the village of Aurahi Hingna, Bihar, India.
 
• Renu is regarded as one of the most prominent writers of post-independence Hindi literature.
 
• His writing style is characterized by the use of regional language and a deep understanding of rural life.
 
• In 1970, he was awarded the **Padma Shri** for his contribution to Hindi literature but returned it in protest against the emergency imposed in India in 1975.
 
 
 
• **Other Works by Phanishwar Nath Renu:**
 
 
• Notable works include **'Parti Parikatha,' 'Juloos,' 'Kitne Chaurahe,'** and **'Adim Ratri Ki Mahak.'**
 
• His short story **'Maare Gaye Gulfam'** was adapted into the classic Hindi film **'Teesri Kasam'** (1966).
 
 
 
• **Aanchalik Upanyas:**
 
 
• This is a literary tradition that focuses on the life, culture, and socio-economic issues of a specific region.
 
• Phanishwar Nath Renu is considered the **torchbearer** of this genre in Hindi literature.
 
• His works reflect a deep empathy for the struggles and aspirations of rural communities.
 
 
 
• **'Maila Aanchal' in Context:**
 
 
• The title translates to **'The Soiled Border'**, symbolizing the struggles and imperfections of rural life.
 
• The novel is semi-autobiographical, drawing heavily from Renu's own experiences in his native region.
 
• It is often compared to the works of Munshi Premchand for its realistic portrayal of rural India.

questions.question: The average separation between the sun and the earth in terms of light years is 8.311 minutes. Here, minutes indicate:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Light travels at a speed of approximately **299,792 kilometers per second** in a vacuum.
 
• The average distance between the Earth and the Sun is about **149.6 million kilometers**, which light covers in approximately **8.311 minutes**.
 
• When we mention "minutes" in this context, we are referring to **the time it takes for light to travel a certain distance**.
 
• This measurement is used to represent **distance in terms of the time taken by light to traverse it**, a common practice in astronomy.
 
• Thus, the term "minutes" in this context symbolizes **distance, not time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light Year:**

 
 
• A light year is the distance that light travels in one year in a vacuum.
 
• It is approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers** or **5.88 trillion miles**.
 
• It is a unit used to measure astronomical distances between celestial objects.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):**
 
 
• The Astronomical Unit is the average distance between the Earth and the Sun.
 
• 1 AU is approximately **149.6 million kilometers**.
 
• It is commonly used to describe distances within our solar system.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Light:**
 
 
• The speed of light is a universal constant, denoted by "c," with a value of approximately **299,792 kilometers per second**.
 
• It is the fastest speed at which information or matter can travel.
 
 
 
• **Time and Distance Relationship in Astronomy:**
 
 
• In astronomy, distances are often expressed in terms of the time light takes to travel (e.g., light-years, light-minutes).
 
• This method makes it easier to comprehend vast distances in the universe.
